Percentages and sums

Source: vignettes/percentages-and-sums.Rmd
percentages-and-sums.Rmd

Two tests check whether reported percentages and sums can have been derived from reported counts:

  • percentage_of() and percentage_of_map() check whether a reported percentage is consistent with a reported count and total.
  • add_up_to() and add_up_to_map() check whether reported counts, such as group sizes, sum to a reported total.

The math is trivial. What the functions add is safe application at scale: the *_map() functions test every row of a data frame, audit() summarizes their results, and percentage_of() handles rounding in exact integer arithmetic, so floating-point error cannot change a result. All of these functions are experimental.

Percentages

Single cases: percentage_of()

40 out of 120 is 33.33…%, so it can be reported as 33 or 33.3, but not as 34:

percentage_of(absolute = 40, percentage = 33, n = 120, digits_percentage = 0)
#> [1] TRUE
percentage_of(40, 34, 120, digits_percentage = 0)
#> [1] FALSE

percentage_of(
  absolute = 40,
  percentage = 33.3,
  n = 120,
  digits_percentage = 1
)
#> [1] TRUE

digits_percentage is required, like digits_x in grim(), since a numeric value does not keep trailing zeros. rounding, threshold, and symmetric work as in grim().

This check is stricter than grim() with x_meaning = "percentage", which only asks whether some count out of n could have produced the percentage. percentage_of() asks about one specific count, so it needs that count to be reported.

Many cases: percentage_of_map()

percentage_of_map() tests every row of a data frame with the columns absolute, percentage, and n:

df <- tibble::tibble(
  absolute = c(40, 37, 25),
  percentage = c(33, 31, 20),
  n = 120
)

df |>
  percentage_of_map(digits_percentage = 0)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#> # Percentage: default settings
#>   absolute percentage     n digits_percentage consistency
#>      <int>      <dbl> <int>             <int> <lgl>      
#> 1       40         33   120                 0 TRUE       
#> 2       37         31   120                 0 TRUE       
#> 3       25         20   120                 0 FALSE

25 out of 120 is 20.8%, which would have been reported as 21, so the third row is inconsistent. audit() summarizes the results:

df |>
  percentage_of_map(digits_percentage = 0) |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   all_cases incon_cases emp_incon
#>       <int>       <int>     <dbl>
#> 1         3           1     0.333

Investigating possible causes of inconsistencies

A FALSE result means that the three values cannot all be correct as reported, not why. The cause might be trivial: the percentage may be based on a denominator other than n, such as the number of valid responses or the sample size before loss to follow-up.

percentage_of_map_seq() varies the counts, percentages, and totals a few steps up and down and tests each resulting value set, as grim_map_seq() does. With var = "n", it shows which nearby denominators would make the percentage consistent:

df |>
  percentage_of_map_seq(digits_percentage = 0, var = "n")
#> # A tibble: 10 × 8
#> # Percentage: var = "n"
#>    absolute percentage     n digits_percentage consistency diff_var  case var  
#>       <int>      <dbl> <int>             <int> <lgl>          <int> <int> <chr>
#>  1       25         20   115                 0 FALSE             -5     3 n    
#>  2       25         20   116                 0 FALSE             -4     3 n    
#>  3       25         20   117                 0 FALSE             -3     3 n    
#>  4       25         20   118                 0 FALSE             -2     3 n    
#>  5       25         20   119                 0 FALSE             -1     3 n    
#>  6       25         20   121                 0 FALSE              1     3 n    
#>  7       25         20   122                 0 TRUE               2     3 n    
#>  8       25         20   123                 0 TRUE               3     3 n    
#>  9       25         20   124                 0 TRUE               4     3 n    
#> 10       25         20   125                 0 TRUE               5     3 n

The nearest consistent total is two steps away: 25 out of 122 is 20.49%, reported as 20.

audit() counts the “hits”, the varied value sets that are consistent:

df |>
  percentage_of_map_seq(digits_percentage = 0, var = "n") |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   absolute percentage     n consistency hits_total hits_n diff_n diff_n_up
#>      <int>      <dbl> <int> <lgl>            <int>  <int>  <int>     <int>
#> 1       25         20   120 FALSE                4      4      2         2
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: diff_n_down <int>

Sums

Single cases: add_up_to()

add_up_to() checks whether counts sum to a total:

add_up_to(c(40, 37, 43), total = 120)
#> [1] TRUE
add_up_to(c(40, 37, 44), total = 120)
#> [1] FALSE

A missing or fractional value gives NA: a fractional count describes no group, and a sum of decimals is not exact in floating-point arithmetic.

Many cases: add_up_to_map()

add_up_to_map() adds up any number of columns, selected with tidyselect syntax as in dplyr::select(), and compares the sum to a total column:

df_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~n_control , ~n_treatment , ~n_waitlist , ~total ,
          40 ,           37 ,          43 ,    120 ,
          25 ,           26 ,          24 ,     75 ,
          31 ,           30 ,          30 ,     90 ,
)

df_groups |>
  add_up_to_map(summands = starts_with("n_"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   n_control n_treatment n_waitlist total consistency
#>       <dbl>       <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>      
#> 1        40          37         43   120 TRUE       
#> 2        25          26         24    75 TRUE       
#> 3        31          30         30    90 FALSE

df_groups |>
  add_up_to_map(summands = starts_with("n_")) |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   all_cases incon_cases emp_incon
#>       <int>       <int>     <dbl>
#> 1         3           1     0.333
